products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer is Heidolph's lightest overhead stirrer at 2.3 kg, delivering 65 Ncm of torque across 20 to 2,000 rpm for viscosities up to 10,000 mPas.
A magnetic stirrer works until the medium gets thick, the volume gets large, or the solids settle. Then it stops working, quietly, and you find out later.
Torque where magnetic stirring gives up. A stir bar decouples in a viscous medium. A driven shaft does not.
The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are NOT included.
features: 65 Ncm of Torque: Torque, not speed, is what decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job.
Keyless Quick-Action Chuck: The Quick Chuck opens and closes by hand, with no key and no tool.
Stirrer Shafts from 0.5 to 10.5 mm: The chuck clamps shafts from 0.5 mm up to 10.5 mm.
Max Button: One press takes the drive to its maximum 2,000 rpm immediately.
Viscosity to 10,000 mPas: The drive handles media up to 10,000 mPas.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically.
Software Motor Monitoring: The motor is monitored in software, and a fault produces an error message.
2.3 kg, the Lightest Hei-TORQUE: The drive can be moved, mounted, and dismantled easily by one person.
Electronic Speed Control to +/-1%: Speed runs from 20 to 2,000 rpm under electronic control.
RS232 Interface: This configuration includes an RS232 interface.
applications: Viscous Media: 65 Ncm of torque drives a shaft through media up to 10,000 mPas.
Suspensions and Slurries: The Max button reslurries settled solids in a short burst.
Larger Volumes: Up to 25 litres in water, well beyond a magnetic stirrer reach.
Homogenisation: A driven shaft with the right element homogenises where a stir bar cannot.
Closed Systems: The 2.3 kg drive can be mounted into closed systems and enclosures.
Fume Hood and Awkward Locations: Light enough to install and dismantle single-handed in tight spaces.
Continuous Stirring: Rated for continuous operation, with a certificate available.

products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Expert-100 Overhead Stirrer delivers 100 Ncm of torque with a live torque trend display, for viscosities to 60,000 mPas.
Most stirring is a black box. You set a speed, you come back later, and you hope the medium did what you expected.
The torque trend bar shows the load the drive is under, so a thickening reaction or a completing dissolution becomes visible while it happens rather than afterwards.
The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are NOT included.
features: Torque Trend Display: A bar indicator keeps the delivered torque visible for the whole run. Changes in the medium can be tracked as they happen, the speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque reliably monitored. This is the feature that turns a stirrer into an instrument that tells you something.
100 Ncm of Torque: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. At 100 Ncm the Expert reaches media six times more viscous than the Hei-TORQUE Core.
Viscosity to 60,000 mPas: The drive handles media up to 60,000 mPas. That covers thick suspensions, gels, and viscous polymer solutions that a lighter drive would simply stall in.

Speed from 10 rpm: The range starts at 10 rpm, lower than the Core's 20 rpm. A viscous medium often needs to be brought up gently, and a drive that cannot go slow enough is as much a problem as one that cannot go fast enough.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.
Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely once clamped.
2.4 Inch Display: Application parameters are set and the process controlled from a 2.4 inch display, including the torque trend bar.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs in demanding media.
90 W Power Input: Despite delivering more torque than the Hei-TORQUE Core, the Expert draws less power, at 90 W against the Core's 105 W.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.
applications: Viscous Media: 100 Ncm drives a shaft through media up to 60,000 mPas.
Monitored Reactions: The torque trend display shows the medium changing as it happens.
Polymerisation: Rising torque is the signal that the medium is thickening.
Dissolution and Suspension: Falling torque indicates solids going into solution.
Fume Hood Work: IP54 and under 50 dB(A), sealed and quiet enough for enclosed working.
Reactor Superstructures: Rated as a drive for reactor assemblies.
Larger Volumes: Up to 50 litres in water.
Gentle Start on Thick Media: The 10 rpm minimum brings a viscous medium up slowly.
Continuous Stirring: Rated for continuous operation, with a certificate available.

body: Torque, viscosity and volume planning explains what 100 Ncm actually reaches, and why the viscosity and volume figures cannot be read together.
Read this before you read any other number on this page.
Heidolph states that the Expert 100 stirs viscosities up to 60,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water. Two separate ceilings on the same 100 Ncm drive. Not a combined specification.
Fifty litres is what 100 Ncm reaches when the medium behaves like water. Sixty thousand mPas is what 100 Ncm reaches when the volume is small. You do not get 50 litres of a 60,000 mPas medium.
The torque trend display is the honest answer to this problem. Instead of trusting a headline figure, you watch the actual torque the drive is delivering and see how much headroom is left.

products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer delivers 200 Ncm with a live torque trend display, for viscosities to 100,000 mPas.
Doubling the torque of the Expert 100 does not get you a bigger vessel. Both drives stop at the same volume. What the extra power buys is a medium that has stopped being pourable.
Viscosity, not volume. This is the drive you move to when the medium is too thick, not when the vessel is too large. The volume ceiling is unchanged from the Expert 100.
You can see what the medium is doing. The torque trend bar shows the load the drive is under, so a thickening reaction becomes visible while it happens.
Still not a complete instrument. The stand, the shaft, and the stirring element are separate items.
features: 200 Ncm of Torque: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. At 200 Ncm the Expert 200 turns media that would stall a 100 Ncm drive, and it does so at the same working volume.
Viscosity to 100,000 mPas: The drive handles media up to 100,000 mPas. That is the territory of heavy gels, pastes, loaded slurries and viscous polymer solutions, where a lighter drive simply stops.

Torque Trend Display: A bar indicator keeps the delivered torque visible for the whole run. Changes in the medium can be tracked as they happen, the speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque monitored reliably. At this end of the viscosity range, headroom is what you are watching.

Speed from 10 rpm: The range starts at 10 rpm. A very viscous medium usually needs to be brought up slowly, and a drive that cannot go slow enough is as much of a problem as one that cannot go fast enough.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.

Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely once clamped. At 200 Ncm, a tool that slips in the chuck is not a minor inconvenience.
2.4 Inch Display: Application parameters are set and the process controlled from a 2.4 inch display, including the torque trend bar.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs in demanding media.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.
applications: High-Viscosity Media: 200 Ncm drives a shaft through media up to 100,000 mPas.
Gels and Pastes: Torque, not speed, is what moves a medium that will not pour.
Polymerisation: Rising torque is the direct signal that the medium is thickening.
Heavily Loaded Slurries: High solids loading raises torque demand sharply.
Monitored Reactions: The torque trend display shows the medium changing as it happens.
Fume Hood Work: IP54 and under 50 dB(A), sealed and quiet enough for enclosed working.
Reactor Superstructures: Rated as a drive for reactor assemblies.
Gentle Start on Heavy Media: The 10 rpm minimum brings a viscous medium up slowly.
Continuous Stirring: Rated for continuous operation, with a certificate available.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer is a Heidolph overhead stirrer used for high-viscosity media and monitored reactions. It delivers 200 Ncm of torque across 10 to 2,000 rpm, for viscosities up to 100,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water, and displays the delivered torque live.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer is 200 Ncm. Torque, rather than speed, determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Torque Expert-100 and the Expert-200?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-200 delivers 200 Ncm against the Expert-100's 100 Ncm, and reaches 100,000 mPas against 60,000 mPas. The maximum volume is the same on both, at 50 litres in water. The extra torque buys a thicker medium, not a larger vessel.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer stir a larger volume than the Expert-100?
faqs.answer: No. Both the Hei-Torque Expert-200 and the Expert-100 have a maximum volume of 50 litres in water. Doubling the torque raises the viscosity ceiling, not the volume ceiling. If your constraint is vessel size rather than medium thickness, more torque will not solve it.

faqs.question: What viscosity can the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer handle?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 100,000 mPas, at reduced volume. That covers heavy gels, pastes, loaded slurries, and viscous polymer solutions.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer stir 50 litres of a viscous medium?
faqs.answer: No. The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 100,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water. These are two separate ceilings on the same 200 Ncm drive, not a combined capability. As viscosity rises, the volume the drive can turn falls.

faqs.question: What is the torque trend display on the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The torque trend display on the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer is a bar indicator that keeps the delivered torque visible throughout the run. Changes in the medium can be tracked as they happen, the stirring speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque monitored reliably.

faqs.question: What shaft diameters fit the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The quick-action chuck on the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer accepts stirring shafts from 2.5 mm to 10.5 mm, and has a safety ring. For shafts thinner than 2.5 mm, the Hei-TORQUE Core goes down to 0.5 mm.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer be used in a fume hood?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer carries IP54 protection and operates below 50 dB(A), and Heidolph rates it for use in fume hoods and as a drive for reactor superstructures.

faqs.question: What is included with the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer is supplied as a drive unit. The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are separate items and are not included. At 200 Ncm the stand and boss head must be rated to hold against the reaction torque, so Inkarp quotes a complete working setup rather than a drive alone.

faqs.question: What is the part number of the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The part number of the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer is 501-62010-00. Inkarp is the authorized distributor for this Heidolph configuration in India.

sections.title: Torque, Viscosity and Volume Planning
body: Torque, viscosity and volume planning explains what 200 Ncm reaches, and why the extra torque does not raise the volume ceiling.
The single most useful thing on this page.
The Expert 200 has twice the torque of the Expert 100. Its maximum volume is the same: 50 litres in water. Only the viscosity ceiling moves, from 60,000 mPas to 100,000 mPas.

That tells you what the extra torque is for. It buys a thicker medium, not a bigger vessel. If your problem is that your vessel is too large, moving up from the Expert 100 to the Expert 200 will not solve it. If your problem is that your medium is too thick, it will.

Heidolph also states these as separate ceilings: viscosities up to 100,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water. Not both at once. Fifty litres is what 200 Ncm reaches when the medium behaves like water. One hundred thousand mPas is what it reaches when the volume is small.

Product expert note Give our team your medium, its viscosity, your working volume, and your vessel diameter, and we will tell you whether the problem you have is a viscosity problem or a volume problem. They have different answers.
